packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET 09 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: No proposed identification of the work or author was revealed to me in my context. The images themselves carry modern pencil labels "Stams, STA, Frg. 77r" (image-001/005) and "Stams, STA, Frg. 77v" (image-006/007), and a modern ink note in the right margin of 77r (image-005, partly read: "...1673."). These are shelfmark/provenance labels, not identifications; I have not used them to identify anything. Nothing done beyond the rules. Images opened: image-001 to image-010 (image-011 does not exist). All loaded.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two faces of one parchment fragment, each an overview + 4 tiles:
  Face A (label 77r): image-001 overview; image-002 = col. a upper + edge of col. b; image-003 = col. b upper; image-004 = col. a lower + edge of col. b; image-005 = col. b lower.
  Face B (label 77v): image-006 overview; image-007 = col. a upper; image-008 = col. b upper; image-009 = col. a lower; image-010 = col. b lower.
- Fragment is a bifolium/leaf section reused in a binding: folded strip at top, fold/crease running vertically between the two text columns, lower margin folded under. Each face shows two text blocks separated by a fold, ~28-29 lines visible per column. Whether the two blocks on a face are two columns of one page or two pages across a fold is not certain from these crops; I call them col. a (left) and col. b (right).
- Single hand, small Gothic-leaning book hand (protogothic look), brown ink, heavy standard abbreviation. No interlinear or marginal glosses by the main hand seen. No commentary/lemma structure: continuous prose.
- Red: running-head-type letters at top of face A (red "M"-like letters / "MIV"? over col. a and "M(?)" over col. b; I cannot read them securely); red numeral "XVI" at top of col. b on face B (image-008 L0, above text). Red-stroked capitals at sentence openings: face A col. a "D(einde)" (image-004 L14), "R" at foot (image-004 L19); face A col. b "D(efuncto)" (image-003 L2), "I/T" at foot (image-005 L18); face B col. b "Q(ui)" (image-008 L3), "Q(uamuis)" (image-010 L6).
- Face A col. b: a pasted paper/parchment slip with different, darker writing ("op[?]iu" / "[?]rixinen" / "..") covers the inner edge of the first lines; a round loss/patch (image-005 lower left) covers line starts lower down. The first 2-4 letters of most col. b lines on face A are lost under the fold/discoloration.
- Face B col. a: severely abraded and stained; over it lies dark mirror-image offset text (reversed letters, larger script, printed or written) running vertically, which obscures much of the column; similar mirror offset in the left margin strip. Treat letters inside that zone as very uncertain. Face B col. b is well preserved.
- Top-right corner of face B (image-008): a black fragment of letters ("III"?) on the turned-over edge, apparently offset/other material.

CONVENTIONS: line numbers counted from top of each image (first text line = 1). Overlap between tiles noted; repeated lines not counted twice. ( ) = expansion; ? = uncertain reading before it; [illegible] / [..] = unread letters.

- Weak/unread: face B col. a is largely obscured by stain and mirror offset; the middle of most lines there is [illegible]. LIMITATIONS
- Column vs. page order across the central fold is uncertain; I have not assumed which face is recto or which block precedes.
- Some expansions are guesses at the abbreviation only (marked ?); I have not supplied words from expected sense.
